findings.message: No test checks that a paid request is 'covered' (and not charged) when the player's own start rumor gives that type in the same step. This is either control start or a late joiner's first step. The branch in packages/simulation/src/intel/step.ts:323 (`entry.type === startType` -> delivery 'free') never runs deterministically. No scripted test sends a request on a start step (intel.test.ts:125-185 starts without requests), and the phase tests call decideLeads without the `starting` argument (intel.test.ts:715). The free-rumor cover test (intel.test.ts:773) only uses a replacement rumor. The property Checker would not catch a regression either. checkCharges (property.test.ts:526) keeps only the last lead per (player, type). So if this branch were removed, a second rumor sent as 'targeted' and charged would pass as 'rumor:targeted'. That would double-charge a late joiner who buys the type their start rumor names, which is the exact charging bug this follow-up exists to fix. Needed: a scripted test (or a decideLeads test with `starting`) where a request on a start step for the start rumor's type is answered 'covered', and the rumor goes out once with reason 'start'.
findings.requirement: `covered` (not charged) if a free trigger already put that player's type in this step's message, or a free rumor for that type in this step

findings.message: The all-orders phase tests (intel.test.ts:683-797) never give gatherLeads two free triggers for the same (player, type). So nothing checks the rule that makes the kept free trigger independent of arrival order: compareFree, step.ts:225/241 (earliest tick first, then 'fresh' before 'replacement'). That case can happen, for example a pending type re-gathered at a boundary alongside a replacement for the same type. Also, the permuted triggers are all at T0, with no earlier-tick pending trigger among them. If gatherLeads kept the first free trigger to arrive, every test would still pass. The black-box permutation check can't catch it either, because stepIntel pushes free triggers in a fixed order in code, not in view-array order.
findings.requirement: Collect every trigger into a set keyed by **(player, type)**, whatever order the triggers arrive in

findings.message: The type-level test (intel.test.ts:797-802) only checks the new alias CarrierSightingReason with @ts-expect-error. It never checks that the sighting's own field uses it (CarrierSighting.reason, state.ts:304). If that field went back to IntelLeadReason, typecheck and every test would still pass. The runtime Checker (SIGHTING_REASONS) would only catch a 'start' sighting if a run actually produced one. The @ts-expect-error should target a CarrierSighting value, or the carrier-sighting message body's reason.
findings.requirement: The sighting's reason type is narrowed to `fresh`, `targeted` and `replacement`, and the property checker rejects anything else.

findings.message: No test has a 'none' group with more than one request. The direct answerRequests test (intel.test.ts:786) uses a single-id 'none' group (['h']). Every multi-request case through decideLeads is 'capped', 'rumor' or 'sighting'. So the requirement that every request of an undeliverable (player, type) gets the same 'none' is only shown for one request. Nothing asserts that none of the others is 'covered' or charged.
findings.requirement: when nothing can be delivered for that (player, type) (for example capped), every request gets the same non-charged result (`capped` or `none`).
